recent_posts.title: Welcoming Abigail Besdin, Mozilla’s new Chief Operating Officer
recent_posts.summary: Mozilla has appointed Abigail Besdin as its new Chief Operating Officer. Besdin brings over 18 years of experience, including co-founding property management startup Great Jones (raising $30M, reaching $10M ARR, and leading its acquisition by Roofstock), serving as Chief of Staff at Roofstock, and spending six years at Skillshare building its online learning platform. As COO, she will oversee Mozilla's Core Services teams including Business Operations, Data, Infrastructure, IT, Legal, People, Security, and Strategy, reporting directly to the CEO.

recent_posts.title: What’s new in Firefox mobile: Less clutter, more control and a free built-in VPN
recent_posts.summary: Firefox is rolling out several mobile updates: Shake to Summarize (AI page summarization, expanding to more languages and Android), AI Controls to manage which AI features are enabled, a free built-in VPN covering 50GB/month of browsing with no ads or data selling, and Tab Groups for organizing tabs with smart grouping suggestions coming soon. Most features are rolling out on Android and iOS between April and May 2025.

recent_posts.title: How Mozilla used AI to find 271 Firefox security vulnerabilities
recent_posts.summary: Mozilla's Firefox team used Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview AI model to identify and fix 271 security vulnerabilities in Firefox 150, following an earlier collaboration that fixed 22 bugs in Firefox 148. The post argues that AI-powered vulnerability discovery is shifting the security landscape from offensively-dominant to one where defenders can finally close the gap. Unlike traditional fuzzing or scarce human expert review, frontier AI models can reason through source code at scale, matching elite human researchers in finding complex bugs. Mozilla believes the finite set of latent defects in software like Firefox can now realistically be found and fixed, giving defenders a decisive advantage for the first time.

recent_posts.title: Mozilla criticizes Microsoft for forcing Copilot on users without consent
recent_posts.summary: Mozilla criticizes Microsoft for forcing Copilot onto Windows users through auto-installs, a dedicated hardware key, and default taskbar pinning — without user consent. This is framed as part of a broader pattern of Microsoft using dark patterns to override user choice, including hardcoding Edge into Windows Search and making default browser changes deliberately difficult. Mozilla contrasts this with Firefox 148's approach, which includes a centralized AI Controls panel with a single toggle to disable all AI features, with preferences that persist across updates.

recent_posts.title: 0DIN is open-sourcing AI security and the hard-earned knowledge behind it
recent_posts.summary: Mozilla's 0DIN AI security team is open-sourcing its AI Security Scanner under Apache 2.0, seeded with 179 community probes covering 35 vulnerability families plus six exclusive bug bounty probes. Built on NVIDIA's GARAK framework, the scanner adds a GUI, automated scheduling, cross-model comparison, and enterprise reporting. It targets prompt injection, jailbreaks, and data extraction across frontier models and open-source LLMs. Six previously undisclosed attack techniques are named for the first time. Mozilla is also offering free enterprise security assessments and a managed Enterprise edition with nearly 500 pre-disclosure probes.

recent_posts.title: Mozilla and Mila announce strategic research partnership to advance open source and sovereign AI capabilities
recent_posts.summary: Mozilla and Mila (Quebec AI Institute) are announcing a strategic research partnership focused on advancing open source and sovereign AI capabilities. This is Mozilla's first partnership with a major AI research lab. The inaugural project targets trust and usability, including private memory architectures for AI agents. The collaboration aims to close gaps in the open source AI stack around trustworthiness, privacy, and multilingual/multicultural support, positioning Canada as a leader in frontier AI that the world can trust.

recent_posts.title: Firefox adds a free built-in VPN with 50 GB monthly data
recent_posts.summary: Mozilla is introducing a free built-in VPN feature in Firefox, offering 50 GB of monthly VPN browsing at no cost. The feature masks users' IP addresses by routing traffic through a proxy network, adding a privacy layer on top of HTTPS encryption. It requires no extra apps or downloads and is activated with a single click. Unlike many free VPNs, Mozilla states it does not sell browsing data or inject ads. The feature is currently rolling out in beta for desktop users in the US, UK, Germany, and France starting with Firefox 149, with broader rollout planned. For full-device protection, Mozilla's paid VPN subscription remains available.

recent_posts.title: Try Tab Notes in Firefox to leave a note on any page
recent_posts.summary: Firefox has launched Tab Notes, a new experimental feature available through Firefox Labs. It lets users attach short notes to any browser tab, visible via a sticky note icon when hovering. Notes are stored locally and never sent to Mozilla, keeping them private. The feature is inspired by user research on task resumption after interruptions. To enable it, go to Settings > Firefox Labs and tick 'Tab notes'. Feedback can be shared on Mozilla Connect or Bugzilla.

recent_posts.title: Split View in Firefox: Two tabs side by side, right where you need them
recent_posts.summary: Firefox 149 introduces Split View, a new feature that lets users place two tabs side by side within the same browser window. Available starting March 23, it can be activated by right-clicking a tab and selecting 'Open in Split View'. The Firefox team shares real-world use cases including trip planning, tax filing, and note-taking while reading. Mozilla is seeking user feedback to guide future improvements.

recent_posts.title: Firefox 148 and 149 new features including built-in VPN and split view
recent_posts.summary: Firefox is rolling out several new features across versions 148 and 149. A free built-in VPN is coming in Firefox 149 (March 24), offering 50GB/month of proxied browsing in the US, France, Germany, and UK. Firefox 148 is the first browser to ship the Sanitizer API, a new web security standard blocking XSS attacks. Other additions include Split View (two pages side by side), Tab Notes, and a renamed Smart Window (formerly AI Window) for AI-assisted browsing. A redesigned Settings page with improved navigation is coming to Firefox Nightly in April. Firefox is also getting a visual refresh with updated themes, icons, and a new mascot named Kit.
